\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نشانی} (neshâni)}{نشانی (neshâni)}]{\fa{نشانی} (neshâni) — an address (formal word)}

\label{lesson:FA-C444-neshani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a tip, then the Persian for to thank.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نشانی}}
\textbf{\fa{نشانی}} (\emph{neshâni}) — \textquotedblleft{}an address (formal word)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{نشانی} \fa{هتل} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{راننده} \fa{دادم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Neshâni-ye hotel râ be rânande dâdam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I gave the driver the hotel's address.
\end{quote}

The formal word for \emph{âdres}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{neshâni} is built from native \emph{neshân} 'sign, mark', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{nišān}, with the ending \emph{-i}. EtymDB lists \emph{neshâni} without older forms.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{neshâni}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{neshâni}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{neshâni}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a tip, then the Persian for to thank, then say \emph{neshâni} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پرس} \fa{و} \fa{جو} \fa{کردن} (pors-o ju kardan)}{پرس و جو کردن (pors-o ju kardan)}]{\fa{پرس} \fa{و} \fa{جو} \fa{کردن} (pors-o ju kardan) — to ask around, to make inquiries}

\label{lesson:FA-C444-pors-o-ju-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to thank, then the Persian for an address.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پرس} \fa{و} \fa{جو} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{پرس} \fa{و} \fa{جو} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{pors-o ju kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to ask around, to make inquiries\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{محله} \fa{پرس} \fa{و} \fa{جو} \fa{کردیم} \fa{و} \fa{خانه} \fa{را} \fa{پیدا} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar mahalle pors-o ju kardim va khâne râ peydâ kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We asked around the neighbourhood and found the house.
\end{quote}

\emph{pors} 'ask' (from \emph{porsidan}) + \emph{o} 'and' + \emph{ju} 'seek' (from \emph{jostan}) + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pors-o ju kardan} is built from two native present stems, \emph{pors} of \emph{porsidan} 'to ask', which EtymDB traces to the PIE root \emph{pre\'{k}-} 'to ask', and \emph{ju} of \emph{jostan} 'to seek', with \emph{kardan} 'to do'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pors-o ju kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pors-o ju kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{pors-o ju kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to thank, then the Persian for an address, then say \emph{pors-o ju kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{پرس} \fa{و} \fa{جو} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To ask around, to make inquiries\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بلد} \fa{بودن} (balad budan)}{بلد بودن (balad budan)}]{\fa{بلد} \fa{بودن} (balad budan) — to know (the way, how to do something)}

\label{lesson:FA-C444-balad-budan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an address, then the Persian for to ask around.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بلد} \fa{بودن}}
\textbf{\fa{بلد} \fa{بودن}} (\emph{balad budan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to know (the way, how to do something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{راننده} \fa{تاکسی} \fa{همه} \fa{کوچه} \fa{های} \fa{شهر} \fa{را} \fa{بلد} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Rânande-ye tâksi hame-ye kuche-hâ-ye shahr râ balad ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The taxi driver knows every lane in town.
\end{quote}

Very common in speech: \emph{râh râ balad nistam} — I don't know the way. \emph{Balad}, a guide, is someone who knows the land.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{balad budan} is built from \emph{balad} 'knowing the way; a guide', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{balad} 'land, country' (EtymDB lists the Arabic word), and the native verb \emph{budan} 'to be'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{balad budan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{balad budan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{balad budan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an address, then the Persian for to ask around, then say \emph{balad budan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گم} \fa{شدن} (gom shodan)}{گم شدن (gom shodan)}]{\fa{گم} \fa{شدن} (gom shodan) — to get lost; to go missing}

\label{lesson:FA-C444-gom-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to ask around, then the Persian for to know.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گم} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{گم} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{gom shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to get lost; to go missing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{بازار} \fa{بزرگ} \fa{گم} \fa{شدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar bâzâr-e bozorg gom shodim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We got lost in the big bazaar.
\end{quote}

\emph{gom} 'lost' + \emph{shodan}. \emph{Gom kardan} is to lose something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gom shodan} is built from native \emph{gom} 'lost, missing', which EtymDB lists, and the native verb \emph{shodan} 'to become'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gom shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{gom shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to ask around, then the Persian for to know, then say \emph{gom shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نشانه} (neshâne)}{نشانه (neshâne)}]{\fa{نشانه} (neshâne) — a landmark, a sign}

\label{lesson:FA-C444-neshane}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to know, then the Persian for to get lost.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نشانه}}
\textbf{\fa{نشانه}} (\emph{neshâne}) — \textquotedblleft{}a landmark, a sign\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مسجد} \fa{بزرگ} \fa{نشانه} \fa{خوبی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Masjed-e bozorg neshâne-ye khubi ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The big mosque is a good landmark.
\end{quote}

Also a sign or symptom: \emph{neshâne-ye bimâri}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{neshâne} is built from native \emph{neshân} 'sign, mark', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{nišān}, with the ending \emph{-e}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
